target_customer: Mobile gamers who play free to play social strategy games
problem: Founders started with a chat app (Chatterous), saw players using it alongside games, and moved to build social games with strong communities.
business_model: Free to play mobile games with in app purchases

founders.name: Eric Diep
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page; press names other co-founders but the YC page does not

founders.name: Wilkins Chung
founders.background_notes: Seedtable says A Thinking Ape was founded in 2008 by Wilkins Chung, Kenshi Arasaki and Eric Diep (https://seedtable.com/startups/A_Thinking_Ape-39P6N8P). Not on the YC page.

founders.name: Kenshi Arasaki
founders.background_notes: Seedtable lists him as a founder; Techcouver names him CEO (https://techcouver.com/tag/a-thinking-ape/). Not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Zynga
competitors.traction_then: Held the top ranked game spot on Facebook from the start of 2009

technical_complexity.rationale: Online multiplayer games with live operations and analytics, standard game engineering with scaling of concurrent users.

defensibility.rationale: Communities in each game gave stickiness but games are easily cloned and rely on app store distribution.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Zynga dominated Facebook games; A Thinking Ape grew independently and says it was profitable and growing every year after its first game in 2009.

market_need_then: Facebook and mobile social gaming were growing fast in 2009; the founders found players using their chat app as a game companion.

identity.voice_and_tone: Culture first voice with values such as Ownership and Have Wonderful Arguments

branding.brand_signature: Employer brand: Great Place to Work certification and an owners manual
branding.community_and_virality: Company brands itself on game communities; workplace awards in 2022 and 2023 per its press page

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive studio name and strong employer reputation, but player facing brand is mostly the individual games.

pivots.why: Founders saw people using the chat app as an extension for games

outcome_analysis: A Thinking Ape started in YC as a chat app, moved into social games in 2009 and says it was profitable and growing every year. Embracer Group acquired it through DECA Games in November 2020, one report putting the price near 105 million while another source says terms were undisclosed, so the price stays unrecorded here.
notes: YC page says founded 2009 and batch Winter 2008; press says 2008. Press names Wilkins Chung and Kenshi Arasaki as co-founders (Seedtable) but they are not on the YC page so they are not recorded as founders here. Funding: Seedtable listing implies an August 2008 seed, no amount or investor found, unverified. Acquisition price 105M from Techcouver conflicts with CB Insights undisclosed; not recorded. Chatterous pivot from a digibc profile. Name origin not found. Founder backgrounds not found. Completeness pass: the August 2008 seed of about $0.2M is recorded from Welcome to the Jungle (single outlet, no investors named). Chung and Arasaki added as co-founders per Seedtable.
